data.why: The repo's own Docs folder contains a real sample Pentacam tangential difference-map screenshot that the tool is designed to accept via drag-and-drop/file-upload, so it is copied as the browser's test upload file.

goals: Upload a Pentacam tangential difference-map screenshot and get the tool to auto-detect the corneal vertex and calibrate the px/mm scale
Extract the 0.00 D effective optical zone (EOZ) boundary and fit an ellipse to measure EOZ area, equivalent diameter, and major/minor axes
Set the programmed optical zone (POZ) diameter and click Analyze to compute the retention ratio (EOZ/POZ)
Mark the pupil center and enter the surgeon's Px/Py centration offset to compute target-referenced decentration (dec_TC) in addition to vertex-referenced decentration (dec_CV)
Add results to the series table and export a CSV of per-eye measurements
Batch-process multiple screenshots at once to produce a CSV and HTML summary report across many eyes

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose accurately: automated EOZ size, retention ratio and dual-reference decentration from Pentacam difference-map screenshots, for single eyes and batches. Its phases, features and cited screens hold up, and the checker replayed every task and feature. It should be fixed before filing: it leaves out the map-direction setting and the quality-flag review the README stresses, buries the ablation-centre choice inside the dec_TC task, and has a few small factual slips.
